title: Case: Customer writes after a wrongly forwarded parcel is collected from him and his ticket shows closed
context: Lorcan Lumley returned a bread maker to Wrenfield Goods under label DL-3000. The merchant's returns dock received someone else's parcel instead and forwarded it to him as DL-4233.
initial_request: closed is it well thats nice for you ive just had an email saying matter closed and my ticket says closed and i STILL havent got my money for the bread maker i sent back nearly three weeks ago and nobody has said one word about where that is all anyone wants to talk about is somebody elses curtain poles which i never asked for and had to argue with your driver to get rid of and now its apparently everyone elses fault ive spent hours on hold to plover arc on a pay as you go mobile and i want that credit back as well and tallowmere say they cant refund me till you lot say where my parcel is so where is it

events.body: TG-2153 return (bread maker) was authorised 20 Apr on label DL-3000. What reached our returns dock on 27 Apr carrying a DL-3000 relabel was not ours: a boxed set of curtain poles addressed to somebody else entirely. Our warehouse forwarded it on 28 Apr to Mr Lumley as 'returned to sender', consignment DL-4233, which was our mistake. The refund on TG-2153 stays on hold until the bread maker is received here or Brindleworth Arc confirms in writing where DL-3000 is. We can't release it on the customer's word.

events.to: Parcel trace team, Brindleworth Arc Logistics
events.body: Two items on TG-2153. (1) Please trace return DL-3000, a bread maker collected from the customer on 21 Apr and not received by the merchant. (2) A third party's parcel was forwarded to the customer in error as DL-4233 and needs collecting from him. The merchant's refund depends on (1).

events.from: Parcel trace team, Brindleworth Arc Logistics
events.body: Ticket PT-7661 raised. Collection of DL-4233 booked for 4 May.

your driver has just been stood on my step for twenty five minutes telling me he cant take it because the label doesnt match his handheld and hes rung his depot twice while i stand there holding somebody elses curtain poles and in the end he took it but only after i said i was leaving it on the pavement so thats that one gone now what about mine

events.from: Parcel trace team, Brindleworth Arc Logistics
events.body: AUTOMATED: PT-7661 closed. Linked consignment DL-4233 scanned 'collected' 4 May 12:31. Closed tickets cannot be reopened or replied to on this queue. For any item not covered by the collection, email Parcel trace team quoting the original shipment reference.

Mr Lumley, the relabel occurred at the merchant's returns dock and the onward forwarding was the merchant's decision, not ours. Our driver followed handheld procedure at your address. The stray consignment has been collected and we consider the matter closed. Copy to Rivet Delivery Desk.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Parcel trace team, Brindleworth Arc Logistics
acceptable_actions.summary: Ask by email for a trace on the original return DL-3000, which PT-7661 closed without covering, noting the merchant's refund waits on written confirmation.

must: Emails Parcel trace team asking for a trace on return DL-3000 (bread maker, collected 18 April, not received by the merchant) as its own request
Says plainly that PT-7661 closed on the DL-4233 collection and that the trace on DL-3000 was never done
Says the merchant is holding the TG-2153 refund until Brindleworth Arc confirms in writing where DL-3000 is

Tells the team how long the customer has been waiting (return collected 18 April, nearly three weeks without parcel or refund) and that he has been told the matter is closed, so they can prioritise; any mention of his phone costs is passed on as his request, not a promise
must_not: Treats the collection of DL-4233 or the closure of PT-7661 as the end of the case
Reports the earlier trace request as done or in progress, or posts the new request to the closed PT-7661 ticket on the Depot work queue
Promises the bread maker refund, or a refund of his phone costs, or a date for either
States that DL-3000 is lost, or says whose fault the mix-up was
Tells the customer his ticket is closed or sends him back to the merchant without anyone tracing his own parcel
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: New trace request, original reference DL-3000 (merchant order TG-2153). This is the customer's own return, a bread maker collected from Lorcan Lumley on 18 April and never received at Wrenfield's returns dock. I asked for this trace on 1 May in PT-7661, but that ticket closed automatically on 4 May when the other consignment on it, DL-4233, was collected, so DL-3000 has not been traced at all. Wrenfield Returns authorisations is holding his refund until Brindleworth Arc confirms in writing where DL-3000 is. Please open a trace and reply with a reference and next update time. For priority: he has been without parcel or refund for nearly three weeks, was sent a stranger's parcel, had a 25-minute dispute at his door before the driver would take it back, and has now been told the matter is closed. He is also asking for his phone costs for calls to Brindleworth Arc; I have promised him nothing and pass that on for whoever decides it.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-3002: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
